blogs.title: Procedural Rights 'In Vacuo': The D.C. Circuit Clarifies When Mandated Agency Action Creates Judicially Enforceable Rights
blogs.description: This post analyzes the court's application of the procedural injury standing doctrine, particularly its reliance on *Summers v. Earth Island Institute*'s prohibition on 'procedural rights in vacuo.' The post examines what it means for a statute to create a procedural right that is sufficiently tied to a concrete interest, and discusses the implications for plaintiffs seeking to compel agency investigations under various statutory schemes.

blogs.title: Investigation Without Information: When Does a Mandatory Investigation Create an Entitlement to Know?
blogs.description: This post focuses on the informational injury doctrine and the critical distinction the court drew between a statutory command to investigate and a statutory entitlement to receive information. The post explores how this ruling fits within the broader informational injury jurisprudence, including *FEC v. Akins* and *Public Citizen v. DOJ*, and considers what statutory language is sufficient to create the type of information entitlement that confers Article III standing.

blogs.title: The Causation Conundrum: D.C. Circuit Applies Recent Supreme Court Precedent to Multi-Agency Enforcement Chains
blogs.description: This post examines the court's causation and redressability analysis, particularly its application of *FDA v. Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine* and *Haaland v. Brackeen* to the multi-agency context. The post discusses how courts should evaluate speculative causal chains when the requested judicial relief depends on subsequent actions by non-party agencies and exercise of enforcement discretion under *Heckler v. Chaney*.

blogs.title: The Unresolved Tension Between Section 1216 and FOIA's Own Enforcement Mechanism
blogs.description: This post explores the significant statutory interpretation question that the court did not reach: whether Section 1216 provides OSC independent authority to investigate FOIA violations, or whether FOIA's own enforcement provision at Section 552(a)(4)(F)(i) limits that authority. The post discusses the district court's resolution of this issue, the policy implications of each interpretation, and how this ambiguity may affect future litigation over OSC's role in FOIA compliance.
